axioms: Resolution-order determinism is sacred: a (phase, category, run) tuple must resolve to exactly one model regardless of which resolver runs.
Two independently-maintained resolvers (bash lib-routing.sh fast-path vs Go internal/routing) will silently diverge on any input unless a shared invariant forces parity.

An unrecognized model string that falls through to tier 0 (TierUnknown) is more dangerous than a hard error because it feeds directly into ordinal safety-floor comparisons and looks like a normal clamp in logs.
Every routing decision must be auditable: routing_decisions must carry enough provenance fields to distinguish a floor-clamp from an availability-fallback from an agency match.
Kernel-stored agency-spec state (agency.models.${phase}) loaded once via ic agency load is stale the moment the spec or plan changes mid-run, with no reload trigger.
The CLAVAIN_RUN_ID-gated skip of the Go fast-path is a load-bearing invariant, not a convenient accident, and depends on env-var propagation across subagent/subshell boundaries.
primitives: resolver path selection (bash vs Go, gated by CLAVAIN_RUN_ID)
failure_mode: Systematically misses retry/escalation state-machine correctness (attempt counting, tier-stepping, oscillation) — assumes resolution is the only surface.
Does not evaluate whether the downstream pass-rate metric is statistically sound; stops at whether routing_decisions produces auditable rows.
Blind to human-transmission/allocation-independence framing and to flow-volume/spillway framing — reasons purely in config-resolution determinism terms.
